previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient, a woman with chronic pancreatitis secondary to vasculitis, was admitted for acute abdominal pain in the epigastrium and right upper quadrant, radiating to the back, worsened by eating, and associated with nausea and vomiting. Her symptoms were consistent with a flare of chronic pancreatitis, though imaging and labs did not show acute complications. She experienced hematemesis likely due to a Mallory-Weiss tear, which had healed by the time of her EGD, showing no active bleeding, ulcers, or masses. Pain was managed with IV and oral hydromorphone, and her diet was advanced as tolerated. She was treated for GERD with omeprazole and famotidine, restarted on vitamin D, and continued her baseline medications including methotrexate, Plaquenil, and agents for orthostatic hypotension. Urinary symptoms resolved without evidence of infection, and microscopic hematuria remained stable. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans for GI, nephrology, and primary care.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old female p/w abdominal pain and inability to tolerate 
PO intake.

1. Abdominal pain: Her pain is likely multifactorial with a 
component of esophagitis (from chronic vomiting and wretching), 
gastritis, chronic pancreatitis, and vasculitis.  The abdominal 
pain also has a component of abdominal wall tenderness from 
repeated wretching and vomiting---the muscles are sore and 
tired. Pain control was achieved with dilaudid.  Over the course 
of her hospitalization, she was converted to PO dilaudid and 
zofran with adequate control of her pain.  She was able to 
tolerate meals at the time of discharge.  

2. Esophagitis/Gastritis: Histological diagnosis from ___ 
biopsies. The patient at one point had no tolerance to even sips 
of water. Repeated wretching and vomiting would likely further 
exacerbate the inflammation of the esophagus and gastric 
membranes.  GI was consulted for assistance in helping the 
patient tolerate PO's again. Strict NPO was enforced for 48 
hours and the patient had much reduced nausea and vomiting. At 
that point introduction of PO intake starting with ice chips, 
water, and jello were successful. PO meds were slowly 
reintroduced as well.  She was discharged on BID pantoprazole 
after consultation with GI, who did not feel that the pt should 
need both PPI and an H2 blocker.  She will need to follow up 
with her gastroenterologist Dr. ___ on ___ at 10:30AM

3. Depression: Continue lexapro/amytryptiline when pt able to 
tolerate PO's again.

4. Postural Tachycardia Syndrome: Continue betaxalol and 
fludrocort.

5. Vasculitis: Continue methotrexate qWk, folic acid and 
plaquenil when tolerate PO's again. A solumedrol taper was 
initiated when it was considered that her abdominal pain could 
be related to her vasculitis.  On discharge, she was started on

folic acid and plaquenil on discharge.
